text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: streaming-decode pods in prod hitting repeated CUDA OOMs and triggering request drops (P1). Auto-alert at 2024-09-16T12:34:48Z. On-call: @sara.

sara: I’m on it, thanks. Can someone post the last 1m error spikes and recent deploys?

mike: looking. spikes line up with 12:29 deploy (frontend change that allowed very large max_tokens in prompt header). 503s up ~18% across streaming cluster.

jen: customer-reports: ACME (tier: enterprise) says ~15-25% of streaming completions were truncated/missing between 12:30-12:40. ticket #INC-4492.

alex: grabbing pod logs now.

alex: logs (from pod streaming-decode-7f6c):
```
2024-09-16T12:31:02.123Z ERROR decode_runner.cpp:412 cuda_runtime_api.cc:77 CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 238M
2024-09-16T12:31:02.124Z WARN session_manager.cpp:210 session aborted, request id=abc-12345
2024-09-16T12:31:02.125Z ERROR stream_proxy.cpp:98 dropping request, reason=OOM
```

ops-bot: Observability: KV cache growth + active generations per GPU spiked from 8 -> 46. Average seq_len went from 512 -> 14k in the top 0.1% of requests.

sara: good catch. This looks like a runaway-generation / max_tokens mismatch. Immediate mitigations: 1) enforce per-request max_tokens at proxy (soft cap 2048) 2) throttle/blackhole high-memory tenants 3) scale decode pool short-term.

mike: I can flip a proxy header enforcement quickly. Pushing hot-config to proxy-admin:
```
POST /admin/config/routes/streaming
{ "enforce_max_tokens": 2048, "action_on_violation": "truncate" }
```

mike: applied. Will return 200 if config accepted.

jen: rolling action to reduce ACME blast radius: enabling tenant-level caps for ACME to 1024 tokens while we investigate.

support: notified ACME that we’re applying temporary caps and that we’ll follow up with a postmortem. They acknowledged.

alex: scaling decode nodes now: `kubectl scale deploy/streaming-decode --replicas=10 -n prod`. Note: scaling may help throughput but not fix unbounded KV/cache growth.

ops-bot: Scale triggered. New replicas coming up. Memory pressure still high on older nodes; some pods still crash repeatedly.

sara: prioritize blocking bad requests at the edge. If proxy enforcement fails for any reason, fallback to returning 429 to avoid OOM cascade.

mike: added the fallback. Proxy will now truncate and add header `x-generation-truncated: true` and set status 200 for truncated streaming, 429 for requests that exceed absolute hard cap 4096.

alex: verified on a canary: sending an intentionally large prompt (seq_len ~24k) results in truncated stream and `x-generation-truncated: true`. No OOM on canary pod.

jen: ACME metrics since proxy change: completion success from 78% -> 96% within ~3m. Request drops down to baseline.

sara: moving to on-call handoff in 30m unless new alerts. @mike you’ll take the handoff after I triage remaining crash loopers.

mike: ack, I’ll wait for handoff.

ops-bot: Crashloop count decreased from 6 -> 2 after proxy changes and scale; memory pressure trending down.

sara: quick TODOs before handoff:
- open postmortem ticket and link INC-4492 (jen)
- add regression test in load-test harness for extreme prompt lengths (alex)
- restrict default max_tokens in client SDK and add server-side validation (mike)
- follow-up with ACME success engineering (support)

jen: created P0 postmortem draft: PM-1843. Added initial timeline and metrics.

alex: pushed a short-term hotfix to runtime: guard allocation path to early-fail on predicted KV growth > 8GB per-session (will throw 429). Plan to replace with smarter eviction next week.

sara: handing off to @mike at 12:50Z. Leaving notes in the channel and the pager. If anything spikes again escalate to SRE lead.

mike: taking over. I’ll monitor for 60m and coordinate the postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state changed to "stabilized" at 2024-09-16T13:00:25Z. Pager cleared.

support: ACME acknowledged the mitigation and requested timeline for a permanent fix. We committed to ETA EOD and to share postmortem.

sara: final notes: root cause = frontend change that allowed unbounded prompt sizes + lack of server-side early rejection. Impact = customer streaming drops/truncation and transient node OOMs. Next steps = enforce server-side token caps, add load-test coverage, add per-tenant guardrails, and schedule follow-up compliance review for enterprise traffic shaping.

mike: will create follow-up tasks and assign owners. Closing thread after handoff.
